name: United Kingdom
description:
A major global hub for finance, culture, and education. The UK combines historical landmarks with modern innovation, offering strong opportunities in London and throughout the country.

## Key Highlights
- Global financial and cultural hub
- World-class universities and education system
- Strong opportunities in finance, tech, and creative industries
longdescription: The United Kingdom is one of the world's most influential nations, comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. London is a global financial powerhouse hosting the London Stock Exchange and major international banks. The UK's education system produces world-leading universities, including Oxford and Cambridge, consistently ranked among the world's best. British culture has profoundly influenced global arts, literature, music, and entertainment. The country boasts exceptional museums, galleries, and cultural institutions accessible to residents. The economy is diverse and strong, with finance, professional services, creative industries, pharmaceuticals, and technology all significant sectors. London's tech scene is rapidly growing, with thriving communities in fintech, biotech, and software development. The NHS provides universal healthcare to all residents. Infrastructure is excellent, with reliable public transportation and modern facilities. The cost of living, especially in London and Southeast England, is among Europe's highest. Brexit has created regulatory changes affecting immigration and business operations that prospective residents and investors must navigate. English is the official language. The UK offers strong career prospects for skilled professionals, particularly in finance, technology, healthcare, and law. The country provides access to European markets and extensive international business networks. Weather is notoriously grey and rainy. UK offers unparalleled opportunities for ambitious professionals and access to world-class institutions, balanced by high living costs and post-Brexit regulatory considerations.

visas.description: The UK Graduate Visa allows international students who have completed a degree at a UK university to remain in the UK for 2 years (3 years for PhD graduates) to work or look for work in any occupation.
benefits: Stay in the UK after graduating
Work in any job at any salary

visas.description: The UK Skilled Worker Visa allows non-UK nationals with a job offer from a licensed UK employer in an eligible occupation to live and work in the UK for up to 5 years.
benefits: Live and work in the UK
Travel in and out of the UK

visas.name: The UK Global (UK)
visas.description: The UK Global Talent Visa is for leaders or potential leaders in academia, research, arts, culture, or digital technology. No job offer is required; applicants need endorsement from a designated body.

visas.name: The UK Short-term (UK)
visas.description: The UK Short-term Study Visa allows non-UK nationals to study an English language course in the UK for up to 6 months (or 11 months if the course is at an accredited institution).
benefits: No CAS required for English courses

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Children of Indonesian citizens automatically acquire Indonesian citizenship. Mixed marriages have special provisions for dual citizenship during childhood.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 5 years legal continuous residence (3 years for retired foreigners, 1 year for investors), Indonesian language, good character, economic stability.

**Processing:** Through Ministry of Law and Human Rights, 4-6 months.

Special Category (Limited).desc: Former Indonesian citizens and their descendants may apply with simplified procedures.

Birthright Citizenship.desc: Children born in Indonesia acquire citizenship if at least one parent is Indonesian or stateless.

tax_advice:
- UK income tax: 0% to 45% (depending on taxable income bracket)
- Corporation tax at 25% (lower rate of 19% for profits under £50k)
- VAT at 20% (reduced rates of 5% and 0% on essentials)
- Non-residents: only UK-sourced income is taxable
- Capital gains: annual exemption of £3,000, then 10-20% depending on asset type
- Dividend allowance of £500 per year for basic rate taxpayers
- ISAs allow up to £20,000 tax-free investment
- Tax residence status critical to determine tax liability
local_tips:
- English widely spoken; no pressure to learn English but appreciated
- NHS (National Health Service) free; register with GP immediately after arrival
- Visa sponsorship essential for most work visas; plan well ahead
- Cost of living very high in London; consider regional alternatives
- Council tax, utilities, and council registration required; budget accordingly
- Driving left-hand side cars; international license required
- Weather grey and rainy; invest in good waterproof gear
